thread:
sasha_support: Hi team — Acme reported a spike of tool-calling failures in production starting ~08:12 UTC, affects their checkout flow. They see 422s with "schema mismatch" and occasional 500s from our tool proxy. Request ID: req_0a9f7d. Logs attached below.

acme_dev: Yep, started failing in prod around 08:10 after a deployment. Customers hit an error page. Example response: `HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity`

acme_dev: full response body: `{"error":"tool_call_validation","message":"expected array for items field, got object","tool":"inventory_lookup","request_id":"req_0a9f7d"}`

sasha_support: Thanks. Can someone from runtime confirm whether the router sent the right tool and payload shape? Looks like the tool expected `items: []` but got `items: {}` after our model call.

raj_engineer: I'm looking. Quick note: yesterday we shipped a router change that prefers local-tool variants for accounts tagged as "fast-path". Might be a mis-routed variant that has a different tool schema. Pulling traces now.

ingest-bot: Trace (req_0a9f7d) found across services: model-proxy -> router-v2 -> tool-proxy-legacy -> inventory-service. Latency 220ms. Router flagged variant=local-inventory-v1.

maria_oncall: If router picked local-inventory-v1 (legacy), that variant still expects `items` as an array. The model output should have an array but apparently produced an object. Do we have recent model changes?

raj_engineer: Checking model logs: a rollout to model-mix-2026-02-18 (sampling 5%) included a prompt tweak that enabled named args in tool calls. The transform layer converted single-item lists into objects for compactness (`[x] -> x`). That would break legacy tool schemas. Repro in staging...

sasha_support: Can you paste repro curl we can give Acme so they can confirm? Also we need immediate mitigation for prod.

raj_engineer: Repro curl (staging mimic):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"model-mix-2026-02-18","input":"lookup inventory for sku:123","tooling": {"enabled": true}}'
```
This returns a tool call payload: `{"tool":"inventory_lookup","args":{"items": {"sku":"123","qty":1}}}` on the bad variant. Expected `"items": [{...}]`.

acme_dev: We can patch client to coerce object->array but we prefer a server-side fix. Impact: intermittent failures when router selects legacy variant. ~5% of calls.

maria_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll router fallback for accounts with tag "fast-path" back to canonical inventory variant; 2) Add a shim in tool-proxy that coalesces object->array when schema mismatch detected; 3) Disable model-mix rollout. Recommend (1)+ (2) short-term.

raj_engineer: I can revert the router rule for fast-path in config manager now. Doing a canary revert first. Patch ETA 15m. I'll also open a quick PR to tool-proxy to add a tolerant parser (object -> [object]) with a feature flag. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/tool-proxy/pull/452

sasha_support: Please update here when revert is live so I can tell Acme. Also need timeline for permanent fix.

ingest-bot: Router config revert applied to 10% of fast-path accounts at 08:36 UTC (change-id cfg_892b). Monitoring.

acme_dev: rolling back to old router fixed errors for some customers immediately. We still see a fraction failing (presumably the other 90%).

raj_engineer: Rolling the revert to 100% now. Also pushing the tolerant-parser branch to staging for QA.

ingest-bot: Router revert fully rolled to 100% at 08:50 UTC. Error rate for Acme dropped from 6.2% -> 0.4% (observed over last 10m).

maria_oncall: Good. For the long-term: we need to enforce a strict tool-call schema contract at the router/model boundary. Suggested actions: add an output transform in model-proxy that validates tool args against the selected tool's JSON Schema and rejects/normalizes calls before they reach tool-proxy. Also add CI tests for the `items` array case.

raj_engineer: Agreed. I'll scope a JIRA: INF-3281 "Tool-call schema validation at model-proxy". Plan: schema registry + pre-flight validation + normalized fallback (coerce small predictable mismatches). Estimate: 2 sprints for full work, hotfix shim in tool-proxy done in a day.

sasha_support: For Acme: I've told them we reverted router rules and are rolling a tolerant parser; asking them to replay failed requests if they want server-side reprocessing. They asked for a postmortem and ETA. Can we commit to a hotfix timeline?

raj_engineer: Hotfix PR ready for review, will merge after one approval and deploy to prod in ~2 hours (depends on oncall). I'll ping for expedited review.

maria_oncall: I'll own the postmortem doc. Sasha, can you collect customer impact numbers and sample request_ids? Also capture billing/exposure.

sasha_support: Will do. Sample request ids from Acme: req_0a9f7d, req_0a9f9a, req_0aa1c2. I'll attach their error screenshots and the curl they used.

acme_dev: Thanks for the quick turnaround. We'll keep watching and will share more traces if anything else shows up.

raj_engineer: Follow-ups: (a) add a unit test for the model transform to avoid `[x] -> x` compaction, (b) add schema registry check, (c) telemetry alert on tool schema mismatch rate >0.5% per account.

maria_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated for now. Keeping thread open until hotfix is deployed and postmortem drafted. :white_check_mark:
